nodes.label: Clean ABAP Style Guide
nodes.rationale: Adapts Robert C. Martin's Clean Code to ABAP; mostly compatible with SAP's ABAP Programming Guidelines and respects DSAG recommendations.

nodes.label: Four-Step Legacy Refactoring Plan
nodes.rationale: Get the team aboard, follow the boy scout rule, build clean islands, talk about it - gradual adoption avoids disputes and accumulates improvements.

nodes.label: Boy Scout Rule
nodes.rationale: Always leave edited code a little cleaner than you found it; small extra minutes accumulate over time.

nodes.label: Clean Islands
nodes.rationale: Fully cleaned small components demonstrate the benefit and form tested home bases for further refactoring.

nodes.label: The Team Rules
nodes.rationale: Teams may disagree and deviate, but should give guidance a fair chance first.

nodes.label: Do Not Mix Development Styles in One Object
nodes.rationale: Mixing legacy and new styles (REF TO vs FIELD-SYMBOL, NEW vs CREATE OBJECT, RETURNING vs EXPORTING) in one object causes confusion.

nodes.label: Avoid Encodings, Hungarian Notation and Prefixes
nodes.rationale: Encoding prefixes (iv_, rv_, lt_) make names needlessly longer; may be better ignored in legacy projects to avoid a breach between old and new code.

nodes.label: Mind the Performance
nodes.rationale: Do not optimize prematurely; ~10% of code accounts for 90% of runtime, so measure first and only then discard selected rules.

nodes.label: Prefer Object Orientation to Procedural Programming
nodes.rationale: Classes segment better and are easier to refactor and test; procedural objects (RFC functions, transaction programs) should just delegate to a class.

nodes.label: Prefer Functional to Procedural Language Constructs
Avoid Obsolete Language Elements
nodes.rationale: Newer alternatives improve readability, keep benefitting from optimizations, and ease onboarding of young ABAPers.

nodes.label: Software Design Patterns (singleton, factory, facade, observer, strategy)
Use Constants Instead of Magic Numbers
Prefer INSERT INTO TABLE to APPEND TO
Prefer LINE_EXISTS to READ TABLE or LOOP AT
FINAL if Not Designed for Inheritance
Split Method Instead of Boolean Input Parameter
Do One Thing, Do It Well, Do It Only
nodes.rationale: Recommended as the most beneficial starting point because it tremendously improves overall code structure.

nodes.label: CX_STATIC_CHECK for Manageable Exceptions
nodes.rationale: Checked exceptions must appear in signatures so consumers are never surprised; in sync with ABAP Programming Guidelines but contradicts Clean Code's preference for unchecked exceptions.

nodes.label: Prefer RAISE EXCEPTION NEW to RAISE EXCEPTION TYPE
Write Comments to Explain the Why, Not the What
Prefer Pragmas to Pseudo Comments
nodes.rationale: Pseudo comments are mostly obsolete and replaced by pragmas for suppressing ATC warnings.

nodes.label: ABAP Doc Only for Public APIs
Use the ABAP Formatter Before Activating
Use Dependency Inversion to Inject Test Doubles
Test Seams as Temporary Workaround
nodes.rationale: Test seams are invasive and entangle private dependencies; use them only temporarily to refactor legacy code into a testable form.
